taxonomy:
Here is a taxonomy of the grid-based logic games, constructed solely from the provided rules:

**Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games**

**I. Games Involving Cell State Modification (Coloring/Shading/Marking Cells)**
    *   **A. Direct Cell Coloring/Shading:**
        *   **Chained Block:** Fill cells, consecutive black cells form "blocks" with numbers indicating their size.
        *   **Heyawake:** Fill cells, painted cells cannot connect horizontally/vertically, numbers indicate painted cells in a room.
        *   **Hitori:** Color cells black, no number appears more than once in a row/column, black cells never touch, white cells form a continuous network.
        *   **Kurodoko:** Color cells black, numbers show white cells from the number to the nearest black cell/frame, black cells cannot touch horizontally/vertically, all white cells must be connected.
        *   **Kurotto:** Fill (color) cells, number in a circle indicates sum of continuous black cells extending from it.
        *   **LITS:** Color four consecutive squares (tetrominoes) in each area, similarly shaped tetrominoes cannot touch (except corners), colored squares form a connected network, no 2x2 or larger squares.
        *   **Norinori:** Place blocks in twos in consecutive black squares, each area must contain two black squares.
        *   **Nurimeizu:** Paint cells to create walls for a maze from S to G, white cells cannot be cut off or form a loop.
        *   **Nurimisaki:** Fill cells, cells with circles remain white "Misaki" (only one adjacent white cell), others black, numbers indicate straight line of white cells from Misaki.
        *   **Nurikabe:** Fill cells, black cells form a continuous wall, white cells form areas around numbers (number indicates white cells in area), black cells cannot form 2x2 squares.
        *   **Nuritwin:** Shade cells, each region contains two blocks of same number of shaded cells, all shaded cells connected, two blocks in same region cannot touch, no 2x2 shaded group.
        *   **Sto-stone:** Fill colored cells, numbers in rooms show continuous black cells, black cells cannot connect across bold lines, "dropped" stones fill bottom half of grid.
        *   **Tilepaint:** Color tiles, numbers with diagonal lines show black cells to the right/downward in line/column.
        *   **Usowan:** Fill (colored) cells, cells containing numbers cannot be colored.
    *   **B. Placing Objects that Modify Cell State:**
        *   **Akari:** Place light bulbs in white squares, numbers show adjacent bulbs, bulbs illuminate to black squares/frame, every white square must be illuminated, bulbs cannot illuminate other bulbs.
        *   **Shakashaka:** Place black "triangles in squares", numbers indicate surrounding black triangles, white parts of grid form rectangles/squares.

**II. Games Involving Line/Loop Drawing**
    *   **A. Single Continuous Loop:**
        *   **Dotchi-Loop:** Draw lines to make a single loop, loop goes through centers of cells, through all white circles, makes right-angled turn in all white circles in an area, does not go through black circles.
        *   **Masyu:** Make a single loop with lines, loop passes through all black and white circles, white circles pass straight and turn next to it, black circles turn in cell and go straight next cell.
        *   **Mid-loop:** Draw lines to make a single loop, loop goes through all black circles with the circle as midpoint of the line segment.
        *   **Moon-or-Sun:** Draw a line to make a single loop, loop goes through each room once, in each room through all moon cells or all sun cells, alternates between moon and sun rooms.
        *   **Nagareru:** Draw a line to make a single continuous loop in a direction, loop goes through arrow cells, direction of loop matches arrows, wind blows from arrows, loop cannot advance against wind.
        *   **Slitherlink:** Connect adjacent dots with vertical or horizontal lines to make a single loop, numbers indicate how many lines surround a cell.
        *   **Suraromu:** Make a single loop with lines, loop passes all "Gates" (dotted lines between black cells/frame) once, starts and ends at open numbered circle (number indicates gates to pass).
        *   **Yajilin:** Draw a line to make a single loop, loop does not pass through black cells or numbered cells, numbers show black cells in direction of arrow, black cells cannot touch horizontally/vertically.
    *   **B. Connecting Pairs with Lines:**
        *   **Numberlink:** Connect pairs of the same numbers with a continuous line, lines go through cell centers, cannot cross, branch off, or go through numbered cells.
    *   **C. Drawing Lines from Objects:**
        *   **Pencils:** Draw lines from the tip of pencils, line length equals number in pencil, line goes through cell centers horizontally/vertically/turning.

**III. Games Involving Number/Symbol Placement/Filling**
    *   **A. Filling Empty Cells with Numbers:**
        *   **Choco Banana:** Fill cells with numbers, blocks contain same number, blocks are rotated/mirror images of each other.
        *   **Fillomino:** Fill in all empty cells with numbers, divide board into blocks, each block contains the same number and that many cells, same sized blocks cannot touch.
        *   **Nansuke:** Fill in all blank cells with numbers from a list, numbers are up-down or left to right, one cell has only one number.
        *   **Ripple Effect:** Fill in all empty cells with numbers, rooms contain consecutive numbers starting from 1, if a number is duplicated in a row/column, space between duplicates must be equal to or larger than the number's value.
        *   **Sudoku:** Place a number from 1 to 9 in each empty cell, each row, column, and 3x3 block contains all numbers from 1 to 9.
    *   **B. Filling Cells with Symbols/Marks:**
        *   **Juosan:** Fill in all cells with a "—" or a "|", numbers in "Territories" show how many more of one symbol they get.

**IV. Games Involving Grid Division/Block Formation**
    *   **A. Dividing Grid into Defined Blocks:**
        *   **Double Choco:** Divide the grid into blocks, each block contains a pair of white and gray areas of the same form (rotated/mirror image).
        *   **Five Cells:** Divide the grid into blocks of five cells, each block contains exactly one square placed on a pre-drawn arrow, arrows pass through at least two blocks.
        *   **Sashigane:** Divide the grid into L-shaped blocks (one block wide), cells with open circles form the knee (bend) in a block.
        *   **Shikaku:** Divide the grid into rectangles, each rectangle contains only one number showing the number of cells in the rectangle.

**V. Games Involving Object Manipulation (Placement/Movement/Connection)**
    *   **A. Placing Numbered Objects:**
        *   **Hebi:** Place numbers 1-5 (snake parts) sequentially connected in white squares, snakes cannot touch, numbers in black squares show nearest snake number in arrow direction.
    *   **B. Connecting Objects:**
        *   **Hashiwokakero:** Connect islands (circles with numbers) with bridges, number indicates bridges, max two bridges between islands, bridges cannot cross islands/other bridges, bridges form continuous link.
    *   **C. Moving Objects:**
        *   **Satogaeri:** Move circles (islands) vertically/horizontally so each "country" contains one circle, numbers indicate cells to pass through, circles cannot cross tracks/other circles.
        *   **Yosenabe:** Move all circles vertically/horizontally into gray areas (arrow tip in gray cell), number in gray area equals total of numbers of circles entering it.
